To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a recombinant Escherichia Coli strain expressing human IL-1 receptor Antagonist in insoluble form has been optimized at the laboratory scale for large-scale growth in 50-1 fermenters and that 2) an efficient purification procedure, based on expanded bed adsorption, has been developed for soluble IL-1ra, which can be easily scaled-up to larger volumes and which does not require any intermediate dialysis or gradient elutions.

a large-scale process has been developed for producing a recombinant cytokine (IL-1 receptor antagonist, IL-1ra) in E. coli, which does not need any protein refolding step and can easily be scaled up to larger fermentation volumes.

the large-scale growth and purification of human IL-1 receptor antagonistic protein has been optimized in a single 50-l fermentation run and the final product, obtained with a yield of 24% (12 g of pure product from a 50-l fermentation), shows full biological activity in both cellular and in vivo experiments with monkeys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of a human cytokine in a microbial system, which can be considered as a model for the large-scale production of other proteins of this class.
the optimization of a large-scale microbial production process of human IL-1 receptor antagonists.
the development of a large-scale, cost-effective and efficient process for the production of human IL-1 receptor antagonists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study provides an efficient and cost-effective method to produce large amounts of soluble, biologically active IL-1 receptor antagonists, starting from a recombinant bacterial strain which produces this protein mainly in the insoluble form.

the recombinant human IL-1 receptor antagonistic protein can be produced at a very large scale with high purity, high yield, and high biological activity, and that it is suitable for pre-clinical and clinical studies.
the recombinant E coli strain expressing the human IL-1 receptor has been optimized to produce large amounts of active protein, which is suitable for preclinical and clinical trials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the production of soluble human IL-1 receptor antagonists in large-scale fermentations has now been achieved with high yields and purity.

the large-scale production of human recombinant IL-1ra in E. coli is a feasible process, which allows obtaining a high yield of active, purified material with no need for denaturation/ renaturation steps.

a recombinant protein which in laboratory studies is expressed mainly in an insoluble form can be obtained in a large amount in soluble form in a 50- 1 bioreactor process, without any need for solubilization or refolding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a large amount of a soluble protein, with no need for denaturation/ renaturation, can be obtained from a microbial fermentation, with no need of a solubilization step.

, in spite of the high amount of insoluble protein produced, the use of an efficient purification procedure can lead to the recovery of a large amount of pure soluble IL-1ra directly from the cell lysate.
a recombinant protein can be produced at large scale in soluble form directly from a microbial fermentation, without any denaturing/renaturing steps.
